question.text:
The given system has infinitely many solutions for $k=?$
$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
2 & 2 & -4 \\
1 & 3 & -2 \\
-4 & k & 8
\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}
x \\
y \\
z
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c}
3 \\
4 \\
-6
\end{array}\right]
$$

  1. $0$
     
  2. $4$
     
  3. $−4$
     
  4. $\text{All real values}$
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
Consider a matrix $A_{4 \times 5}$., where all the solutions of $A x=0$ has the following form :
$$
\left[\begin{array}{c}
6 c-12 e \\
-4 c+10 e \\
c \\
-5 e \\
e
\end{array}\right]
$$
What will be the rank of $A?$
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
Let $A$ be a $2027 \times 2027$ real skew-symmetric matrix (i.e., $A^T = -A$).

Evaluate $\det(A)$.

  1. $1$
     
  2. $-1$
     
  3. $0$
     
  4. Non-zero real number
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
Let $A_n$ be an $n \times n$ matrix where the entry in the $i$-th row and $j$-th column is given by $a_{ij} = \min(i, j)$.

Evaluate the determinant of $A_n$.

  1. $n!$
     
  2. $1$
     
  3. $0$
     
  4. $n$
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
Let $P$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix such that $P^2 = P$ (i.e., $P$ is an idempotent matrix).

Which of the following relationships is always true?

  1. $\det(P) = 1$
     
  2. $\text{Tr}(P) = \text{rank}(P)$
     
  3. $\text{Tr}(P) = n$
     
  4. $\text{rank}(P) = n$
question.subject: Linear Algebra
